replies.user_post: Self custody eliminates exchange risk. It doesn't eliminate security risk. Who generated your seed? On what machine? Could you recover without the vendor's app?
replies.reply: @PROTOCOLNULL @ForecastQuant Spot on. Self-custody protects ownership, not privacy. A fresh receive address for each payment helps, and coin control (picking which UTXOs you spend) stops old history leaking into new payments.
replies.draft: So the practical version is a new address per payment, and choosing which UTXOs you spend so old and new history don't get merged. Do most wallets make coin control easy enough, or is that where people give up?
replies.draft_alt: Good addition. Fresh addresses are easy. Coin control is the part most people skip because their wallet hides it.

replies.user_post: Self custody eliminates exchange risk. It doesn't eliminate security risk. Who generated your seed? On what machine? Could you recover without the vendor's app?
replies.reply: @ForecastQuant Third question worth adding: what does your address reveal once someone links it to you? Self-custody keeps the coins yours, not the history private.

replies.draft_alt: Agreed. Self-custody answers who controls the coins, not who can see them.
